bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Demand cyclicality and weather/labour-linked volatility — MD&A notes cement industry growth slowed to 4-5% in FY2026 (versus prior double-digit growth), partly due to a long monsoon season and labour shortages, indicating exposure to weather and seasonal-labour disruption.
- Loss of operating capacity at Visaka Cement Works — The Directors' Report states the company's other plant, Visaka Cement Works, has stopped production operations as it falls within city limits, making it difficult to run, permanently constraining the company's operating footprint to the Dachepalli plant.
- Macro/regulatory/input-price sensitivity (cautionary statement) — The MD&A cautionary statement flags global and domestic supply-demand conditions affecting selling prices, input availability and prices, changes in government policies/regulations and tax laws, and litigation/industrial relations as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.
- Concentration on, and financial dependence on, the promoter/holding company — The company relies on its holding company, Sagar Cements Limited, for loans, sale of clinker, purchase of spares/coal, and corporate guarantees, creating significant related-party concentration; a material related-party transaction resolution for dealings with Sagar Cements Limited is also being placed before members.
- Execution/completion risk on the ongoing modernisation-expansion project — The clinker and cement-grinding capacity expansion at Dachepalli is still in progress (civil works, ducting/bag-filter fabrication, and phased receipt of indigenous and imported equipment were ongoing at year-end), with completion targeted only by end of September 2026, exposing the company to execution and timeline risk on a capacity-critical project.
- Funding risk on the expansion project after the Rights Issue was not pursued — The Board-approved Rights Issue of up to Rs.180 crores intended to part-finance the expansion and meet Minimum Public Shareholding was not taken forward due to prevailing capital market conditions, leaving the project reliant on equity/internal accruals and bank/institutional borrowings instead of the planned equity route.
- Corporate-structure uncertainty from the proposed merger with the holding company — The Board has given in-principle approval for merging the Company into its holding company, Sagar Cements Limited, subject to regulatory and other approvals, creating uncertainty over the Company's standalone corporate structure and continuity.

business.body: Andhra Cements Limited manufactures and sells cement and clinker, reported as a single operating segment. Its plants are located at Dachepalli (Sri Durga Cement Works) and at a second site (Visaka Cement Works), both in Andhra Pradesh, and it sells clinker to and buys inputs from its holding company, Sagar Cements Limited.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- Sagar Cements Limited — related party: Holding company of Andhra Cements Limited; counterparty for related-party transactions (purchases, loans, sale of clinker, corporate guarantee) and subject of a members'-approval resolution for material related-party transactions.
- Sagar Cements (M) Private Limited — related party: Fellow subsidiary within the Sagar Cements group.
- RV Consulting Services Private Limited — related party: Enterprise in which a KMP of the Company exercises control; counterparty for purchase of property, plant & equipment and for loans.
- Panchavati Polyfibres Limited — related party: Enterprise in which a KMP of the Company is a director or member; counterparty for purchase of packing material.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The company's Sri Durga Cement Works plant at Dachepalli, Andhra Pradesh (grinding operations re-commenced 12th April 2023) is undergoing a Board-approved (24th January 2024) modernisation/expansion project to raise clinker manufacturing capacity from 1.65 MTPA to 2.30 MTPA and cement grinding capacity from 1.82 MTPA to 3 MTPA, together with a new 6-stage preheater system and related equipment modifications/replacements to optimise fuel cost, at an estimated cost of around Rs. 47,069 lakhs to be met through equity/internal accruals and borrowings from banks/institutions. The new preheater was completed and commissioned on 23rd October 2025; civil works for the Cement Mill building were targeted for completion by May 2026; fabrication for ducting and bag filter was in progress; and indigenous and imported main equipment were to be received in a phased manner before end-June 2026, with the overall project expected to complete by end of September 2026. A related proposal (approved 28th March 2024) to raise up to Rs. 180 crores via a Rights Issue, intended to part-finance this expansion and help achieve Minimum Public Shareholding, was not pursued due to prevailing capital market conditions notwithstanding receipt of regulatory approval (valid till 16th December 2025); Minimum Public Shareholding of 25% was instead achieved via an Offer for Sale by the promoter, Sagar Cements Limited, which reduced its holding from 90% to 75%. The company's other plant, Visaka Cement Works, remains non-operational as it falls within city limits, making it difficult to run.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Cement industry growth slowed to 4-5% in FY2026 (from double-digit growth in prior years), attributed to a long monsoon season and labour shortages.
- Medium-to-long term industry outlook pegged at 7-8% per annum growth, broadly in line with GDP growth.
- Infrastructure segment demand remains strong, driven by increased government spending.
- Housing, which accounts for 55% of cement demand, is expected to grow steadily on rural housing expansion, favourable monsoons, moderating inflation and urban real estate activity.
- Government emphasis on affordable housing and mega infrastructure projects (highways, railways, industrial development) expected to sustain cement demand.
- Pent-up demand, a renewed capex push and sustained housing-sector momentum expected to drive demand, with a brief slowdown anticipated in FY2026 followed by robust growth.
- RBI repo rate cuts expected to lower borrowing costs and stimulate spending/investment; new tax structure expected to boost household consumption, savings and investment, both seen as favourable for the cement sector.
- Industry-wide consolidation trend (larger firms acquiring smaller players) expected to continue, aimed at optimising operations, cutting costs and improving pricing power.
- Industry-wide shift toward sustainability (energy efficiency, clinker substitution, grid decarbonisation) and circular-economy adoption (fly ash, blast furnace slag, silica fume) as structural demand/cost drivers.
